info.title: graphwing
info.description: Local node catalog for Rewst Graph. Deterministic git/gh/file/units/herdr/stack/port plus allowlisted scripts and tests. rrRun is an optional plugin when rr.json is present. One-job agent loops return 202 + job_id; completion POSTs an artifact receipt to response_webhook_url (action.wait.webhook). Cloud GitHub/Shortcut stay Rewst integrations. PR driver is a Graph of these nodes, not one agentRun. Public server URL is written by named-tunnel setup (cloudflared-meta.json) or GRAPHWING_PUBLIC_URL; catalog default is loopback.

Fire a Rewst webhook trigger. This host holds the trigger URL and shared secret, so the caller never needs the webhook key.
Deterministic class×size lookup: launcher, model, turns, budget, opposing reviewers. Never picks a vendor because tests were red.
After the map is empty: run a named tests.json recipe. Green or skip ends. Fail auto-adds a ticket from FAIL: lines, drafts if the log is a blob, parks after 3 reds.

Open a versioned pre-PR build under $GRAPHWING_HOME and return its build_id, stage, and next allowed action. Re-posting the same build_id with identical input returns the existing build (created=false); different input is an idempotency conflict.

Apply one durable transition. event_id makes it idempotent: same id + same payload replays the receipt, same id + different payload is 409 idempotency_conflict. holder takes a lease so a second Rewst run cannot advance the same build until it expires. A head, worktree, or state-version the build cannot explain parks it with a named reason.

409.description: invalid_transition, idempotency_conflict, lease_held, or a park

post.summary: Reserve one initial or correction writer turn before an agent exists. The event id makes the claim idempotent, the holder takes the build lease, and the job budget is charged atomically with the durable reservation. A replay returns the original claim; malformed input, conflicting reuse, held leases, wrong stage, exhausted budget, and persistence failure all fail closed without launching a writer.

200.description: claim reserved, or the same claim replayed with replayed=true

400.description: malformed JSON, unknown fields, or invalid build_id, event_id, holder, kind, or lease_seconds; no claim is written

409.description: idempotency_conflict, lease_held, writer_claimed, claim_not_due, no_writer_session, no_job_budget, budget_exhausted, identity mismatch, or a parked build; no new writer is launched

500.description: the durable claim could not be persisted; the operation fails closed

post.summary: Create or recover the one deterministic local Hermes writer job owned by build_id plus claim_id. The initial claim already reserves its stable session; correction claims resume the bound session. Replays attach their webhook to the same job and never launch another.

202.description: the one writer job is queued, running, or already terminal

post.summary: Validate one terminal local writer receipt against the current claim, deterministic job, bound session, and worktree boundary. Initial success transitions writing to verifying once. Correction success consumes the claim and returns to deterministic checks without asserting a gate. Error and timeout preserve files and record recoverable correction state.
Apply only the pending gate transition justified by authoritative check or review receipts already stored for the current change. The caller cannot name an outcome or target.

get.summary: Read a build back from disk. Survives a service restart: stage, receipts, writer session, stacks, evidence rounds, and remaining budget all come from the state document, not memory.

The shared mechanical-and-sensitive stage switch. Reads durable state and the change currently on disk, names the one step this invocation may run, and server-selects the next required review role and reviewer. Read-only: safe to call from a run that is about to be abandoned. 409 means parked or not on this path.

post.summary: Everything that must be true before a writer is allowed to exist: every declared recipe name resolves, resolves to this build's worktree, and is not hook-only; the route carries every launch stamp; the branch is not trunk; the worktree has no unmerged paths and no pre-existing tracked changes. Read-only — a failure is a 409 the caller can fix and retry, not a park.

409.description: one or more preflight failures; see failures[]

post.summary: The writer's whole world: the approved ticket text, the named recipes that will judge it, and the instruction to stage but never commit. Composed server-side so 'only the approved ticket' is a property of the code rather than of a graph template. Read-only and available only behind the current writer claim; claim owns the budget charge.

409.description: missing_ticket, missing_route_stamp, no_writer_session, or a budget park

post.summary: The deterministic gate. Fast checks run in the build worktree. Integration first requires an exactly staged candidate, freezes its tree as an unreferenced deterministic commit, provisions a per-attempt detached worktree under a declared clean git-worktree runner root, verifies the checked-out tree, and runs every recipe there. Never treats a queue acknowledgement as a pass.

200.description: every required recipe reached a verdict; ok says whether they passed

202.description: queued for webhook delivery. ok is false: this is a receipt for accepting the work, not for passing the gate.

409.description: no_recipes, unknown_recipe, recipe_wrong_worktree, hook_not_coverage, not_a_clean_stack, stack_unhealthy, or a park

post.summary: Run the one server-selected micro-review due for this change. Mechanical uses the behavior-and-test lens. Sensitive runs Terra for behavior and tests, then Grok for security and tenant isolation; both roles must PASS the same change and evidence identity. Provider silence is retried and returned as no_verdict with finding=false, with no review round written. With response_webhook_url delivery is async and answers 202 with ok=false.

200.description: the reviewer finished. ok=true is PASS; ok=false with finding=true is a correction turn; ok=false with no_verdict=true is provider silence.

202.description: queued for webhook delivery. ok is false: an acknowledgement is not a verdict.

post.summary: Commit and push exactly once from a durable, versioned finalization intent. After every current-candidate gate passes, the operation persists state=prepared with the event fingerprint, verified parent, candidate tree/change id, branch, remote, exact message, and git authoring boundary before invoking git commit. It then persists state=committed with the verified SHA and immutable commit fields before pushing that SHA as an explicit refspec. A retry may adopt live HEAD only when every prepared field matches; after an uncertain push it verifies the remote branch and completes without recommitting or force-pushing. state=pushed and pr_ready are written together, and replay returns that exact receipt.

200.description: committed and pushed, or replayed when replayed=true

409.description: invalid_transition, not_ready, lease_held, idempotency_conflict, finalize_in_progress, finalize_adoption_mismatch, nothing_staged, commit_failed, push_failed, remote_unreadable, or another fail-closed park

500.description: A prepared, committed, or pushed receipt state write could not be made durable. The same event_id is safe to retry; a pre-commit failure creates no commit, a post-commit failure adopts only an exact match, and a post-push failure verifies the remote before completing.

post.summary: Durably register a launched Rewst source run before monitoring starts. Maps source_run_id to build_id, event_id, workflow_id/workflow_version, expected_stage, deadline, and the exact saved plan_pane, so a run that fails before declaring any output is still supervised and every later report has one destination. Re-posting the same source_run_id with identical input returns the record (registered=false) and repairs a source-run index entry an interrupted registration left missing (index_repaired=true); different input is 409 registration_conflict.
Bind one acknowledged local job to an existing registered source run. Only null to a valid job id or an exact replay is accepted; a different job id is 409 job_binding_conflict.

Reconcile one terminal source-run completion delivered by trigger.workflowCompleted. Deduplicates on source_run.id plus the listener slug, so a republished listener replays rather than re-decides. Requires a matching launch registration, and treats Rewst `completed` without Graphwing's own terminal receipt as workflow_fault rather than success. Retry class comes only from trusted terminal status. Circuit identity starts with registered workflow ID/version, uses strict node/code metadata when the authenticated listener actually has it, and otherwise uses canonical unknown plus terminal status/error presence. Returns 200 for every reconciled delivery, including a park: the action field carries the outcome so the listener can route without a wait node. Send error.present only; a raw message, trace, or body is refused with raw_error_forbidden.

200.description: reconciled; read action and resolution. ok=false with parked=true is a park, not a transport failure.

404.description: unknown_source_run: no launch registration, so the run is not supervised

409.description: idempotency_conflict, registration_conflict, self_listener, or unreadable supervisor state

post.summary: Start or join one durable server-owned watch for the local job already bound to a registered source run. The request carries only stable identity; registered event, job, deadline, and plan pane are authoritative.

get.summary: Read the saved planning-session reports and circuit state for a build. Every retry, park, and circuit-open outcome is recorded here with source run id, workflow version, available failed-node label or canonical unknown, build stage, local job status, action taken, and the exact next operator action. There is no idle human wait anywhere in the path: the report is durable and fetched, never waited on.

repo.name: repo
repo.description: Allowlisted short name, not a filesystem path. Default riftwing.
Allowlisted short name, not a filesystem path.

branch.description: Branch name. Rejected if it looks like a path.

create.description: If true, git checkout -b. Not git checkout -B.

repo.description: Allowlisted short name, not a filesystem path.

clean_untracked.description: If true, remove untracked files and directories with git clean -fd. Gitignored files are retained.

repo.description: Allowlisted short name, not a filesystem path.

add.description: Relative paths to git add before commit, or a single path string. Omitted: commit already-staged files only. No .. or absolute paths. Default does not add -A.

repo.description: Allowlisted short name, not a filesystem path.

remote.description: Named remote already on the repo. Not a URL. Not --force.

ref.description: HEAD if omitted. No +, no :, no delete, no force.

name.description: scripts.json name only. No client argv.

supervised_source_run_id.description: Optional registered source run. The newly persisted async job is bound under the supervisor lock before 202 and before enqueue.

response_webhook_url.description: https URL from action.wait.webhook pending.resumeUrl. Used when the script is async.

response_webhook_token.description: From action.wait.webhook pending.resumeToken. Sent as X-Rewst-Token on the callback.

compact.description: Short test/script failure signal for a resume prompt. 'ok' when the recipe passed. Never the full log.

kick_url.description: https Rewst webhook to start the next slice. Omitted: return frontier only.

test.description: tests.json name. Omitted or empty: skip.

BuildVerification.description: Verification the plan declared for this build. Names are recipes from tests.json, scripts.json, or rr.json, resolved in that order. Every name is validated by buildPreflight before a writer is launched.

needs_visual_proof.description: False skips the evidence stage. A mechanical build that sets this true parks. A sensitive build surfaces step=evidence for the separate visual-evidence path; both sensitive reviews remain required afterward.

requires_red.description: When true the reviewer treats a missing record of the test failing first as a finding. When false or absent the reviewer is told explicitly not to raise its absence.

path_rules.description: Changed-path rules. Add-only by construction: a rule contributes recipe names to the required set for a phase and has no shape that removes a declared one, so a plan cannot use a rule to drop a check it promised.

match.description: fnmatch glob against repo-relative changed paths.

human_review.description: Required explicitly; there is no default.

allow_login_redirect.description: Explicitly permit only a same-origin loopback redirect to a login/sign-in/auth path; probes never follow it.

planning_pane.description: Required by the server when human_review=true.

BuildRecipeVerdict.description: One recipe run to completion. There is no shape here for 'queued' or 'skipped': a command that never ran comes back ok=false with a code, because the alternative is a gate that reads an acknowledgement as green.

coverage.description: False for a recipe that may run but can never make a phase covered, such as a pre-commit hook.

cwd.description: Where it actually ran. A verdict that cannot name its own directory cannot be audited for the failure that looks exactly like success.

code.description: Present only when the command did not produce an ordinary exit: missing_binary is the skipped case, timeout is the ran-too-long case. Neither is a pass.

BuildNext.description: BuildState plus the one step this invocation may run.

ok.description: False when the step is parked.

step.description: Read off the durable document and the change on disk, never from the caller. That is what makes a replay safe: a run that died after its writer finished comes back, is told fast_checks, and does not start a second writer.

step_reason.description: Why this step and not another, in a sentence a human can act on.

finding.description: Non-empty only on step=fix: the exact correction text to pass to buildBrief. Composed from durable state, so a resumed writer sees the same finding whether the run that produced it is alive or died an hour ago.

class.description: The routed class on this shared path. Visual-only builds are refused with not_on_path.

review_role.description: The review lens due when step=review, selected from durable state by the server.

review_reviewer.description: The route-stamped reviewer for review_role. Sensitive routing fixes behavior to Terra and security to Grok.

reviews_outstanding.description: Every missing, negative, non-independent, or stale-evidence review acknowledgement.

visual_outstanding.description: Visual proof or human approval still owed for this exact change.

change_id.description: head plus a hash of the staged and unstaged diff. The writer stages and never commits, so HEAD alone cannot tell one round of the correction loop from the next; every check and review receipt is keyed on this instead.

kind.description: Design resumes the saved writer for exact human visual feedback and does not count as a correction.

worktree.description: Optional assertion; compared with the build's allowlisted worktree.

failures.description: Every failure, not just the first, so one round-trip tells the caller everything to fix.

finding.description: Correction text from buildNext. Present makes this a correction turn and requires the build's recorded writer session; the claim already charged the job budget.

prompt.description: The approved ticket, the named recipes that judge it, and the instruction to stage but never commit. The slice index and the neighbouring tickets are deliberately absent: a prompt assembled from templates acquires them one convenient interpolation at a time, and the writer starts solving the epic.

only.description: Narrows what is executed, never what is required. A correction turn that touched one file reruns that file's recipes and inherits the rest from verdicts already recorded against this same change; a recipe with no verdict at all still runs, whatever only said. Naming a recipe the phase does not require is 400 not_required.

stack.description: Required for phase=integration. Must declare role=clean and runner=git-worktree; arbitrary healthy developer stacks are rejected.

ok.description: The gate. True only when every required recipe reached a passing verdict against this change and at least one of them is coverage. False on a 202.

runner.description: Exact cwd where recipes executed; integration uses an attempt-owned disposable worktree.

materialization.description: Unreferenced synthetic commit whose tree is candidate_tree.

required_because.description: Per recipe, why it is required: 'declared', or 'path:<glob>' for one a changed path mandated.

ran_in.description: Per recipe, the directory it ran in. A catalog default of '.' resolves to $GRAPHWING_HOME, the deployed service rather than the branch under test, so the build re-points it at its own worktree and reports where it landed.

missing.description: Required recipes with no verdict against this change. A non-empty list is never a pass.

reviewer.description: Optional mechanical override. Sensitive review roles and reviewers are selected by the server from durable state; a conflicting assertion is refused.

ok.description: True only on PASS. False on a 202 and false on silence.

evidence_id.description: Identity of the visual evidence set acknowledged by this review, or none when no visual evidence is required.

no_verdict.description: The reviewer ran out of turns or lost its connection. Nothing is recorded and finding stays false: treating silence as a finding resumes the writer to fix a problem nobody reported, spends a round of budget, and does it again next time.

finding.description: A reviewer that finished and still said no. This is a correction turn, not a terminal failure.

BuildFinalizeIntent.description: Versioned durable journal for the one finalization this build permits. prepared exists before git commit and has no SHA; committed adds the inspected commit identity before push; pushed is persisted atomically with pr_ready. A different event cannot take over any state.

sha.description: Absent in prepared; required by committed and pushed state.

notes.description: Stored byte-for-byte as supplied. Whitespace is not normalized.

note.description: Required for split; optional explanation for other decisions.

event_id.description: Names this one finalization. Reuse it to retry safely; the recorded receipt comes back and no second commit is made.

holder.description: Lease owner, normally the Rewst run id. Rejected with secret_in_holder if it carries a credential.

message.description: Persisted and compared exactly. Conflicting reuse is idempotency_conflict; overlong input is message_too_long.

remote.description: A named remote. A URL or a flag is refused with bad_remote.

build_id.description: Caller-chosen id, 8-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9._-]. Required: the caller is the only party that can repeat it, so a generated id would turn every timed-out retry into a second build with its own lease and budget.

story.description: Rejected with secret_in_story if it carries a credential: identity fields are refused, not redacted.

repo.description: Allowlisted short name. The build's worktree identity is that repo's path.

head.description: Git object id the build starts from.

worktree.description: Optional assertion; must equal the allowlisted repo path.

index.description: Optional: omit the key for no index. When present it must be a non-empty repo-relative path of at most 256 characters (BUILD_NAME_MAX), because a later stage opens it inside the build's worktree. null, an empty string, and a non-string are refused with bad_index rather than folded into absent. The service additionally refuses an absolute path, a leading ~, a backslash, and any '..' segment; that rule is enforced server-side, not by this schema.

ticket.description: Optional: omit the key for no ticket. When present it must be a non-empty repo-relative path of at most 256 characters (BUILD_NAME_MAX), because a later stage opens it inside the build's worktree. null, an empty string, and a non-string are refused with bad_ticket rather than folded into absent. The service additionally refuses an absolute path, a leading ~, a backslash, and any '..' segment; that rule is enforced server-side, not by this schema.

route.description: sliceRoute row: launcher, model, reviewers, turns.

event_id.description: Names one requested transition. Reuse it to retry safely.

holder.description: Lease owner, normally the Rewst run id. Rejected with secret_in_holder if it carries a credential: redacting it would make two callers compare equal and share a lease.

release_lease.description: Drop the lease after this transition instead of holding it.

jobs_spent.description: Default 1, or 0 for park. Overrunning jobs_max parks the build.

expect.description: Guards. A mismatch parks the build rather than guessing.

head.description: Optional. Compared to the live worktree HEAD, never to the stored document.

branch.description: Optional plain ref name. Compared to the branch the allowlisted checkout is live on, not to the branch recorded on the build; a mismatch parks with branch_mismatch. Rejected with bad_expect_branch if it is not a plain ref name.

worktree.description: Optional assertion; compared to the worktree the build was opened on.

data.description: Transition payload. Secret-shaped keys and values are redacted before the write. Branch and head identity come from the live Git read of the allowlisted checkout, so no payload field can move them: a data.head is ignored. Unknown keys are dropped. The fields that fold into state are writer_session (a gwslice-<32 hex> session id, bound by start_writer only), stacks, round (evidence_captured), pr (pr_opened), and reason/detail (park). Review authority comes only from buildReview plus buildGate, never data.review.

event_count.description: Event ids this build will never accept a second time. Receipts age out; this count does not.

event_capacity.description: Ceiling on event_count. Reaching it is 409 event_history_full, not an eviction.

created.description: buildCreate only. False when the build already existed.

replayed.description: buildAdvance only. True when the event_id had already run.

base_head.description: Where this build started. head moves when finalization commits, so it cannot answer 'what has this build changed'; the changed-path rules need a fixed floor to diff against.

checks.description: The last recorded run of each phase, keyed fast and integration. Each entry carries the change_id it was recorded against, so a correction turn's new diff leaves it visibly stale rather than silently reusable.

pr_ready.description: The finalization receipt: one per build, forever. Its presence is what makes a second finalize impossible regardless of event_id, so the id is not what makes replay safe.

pending_finalize.description: The durable prepared/committed/pushed finalization intent exposed for recovery and operator diagnosis.

registered.description: False when the same source_run_id was already registered with identical input.

index_repaired.description: True when this identical retry found the launch record present but the source-run index entry missing, and rewrote it. That is the state an interrupted registration leaves behind, and nothing else repairs it.

source_run_id.description: The Rewst run id. This is the external dedupe and correlation key for every later completion, so it is registered before the run can be monitored: a run that fails before declaring any output is still supervised.

build_id.description: An already-open pre-PR build. Registering against a build that was never opened is 404 unknown_build.

event_id.description: The buildAdvance event id this run is launched to record. Reconciliation looks for exactly this id in the build's event history; finding it is the terminal receipt.

workflow_version.description: Half of the circuit-breaker signature: the same version failing at the same node twice opens the circuit.

expected_stage.description: The stage the build must still be in when the completion lands. A build past it that never recorded event_id is a state/trace disagreement and parks.

deadline.description: UTC instant like 2026-08-25T13:00:00Z. An instant, not a duration: a duration would silently extend on every retried registration.

job_id.description: Optional. The local writer/test/reviewer job this run durably claimed. Present-but-missing on disk is what tells a claimed-never-started job apart from an unclaimed event.

plan_pane.description: Required exact herdr pane id for the saved planning session that receives retry, park, and circuit-open reports. Registration rejects a missing, malformed, or unknown pane and never falls back to another tab or the graph dashboard.

SupervisorContinuationSpec.description: Validated non-secret input sufficient for one bounded source invocation. Persisted at registration and returned only in a reconciliation continuation result.

SupervisorContinuationResponse.description: Strict runtime response for one bounded source continuation. It combines the registered invocation with every routing field consumed by the listener graph.

listener_id.description: Listener identity, normally slug@published-version. Only the slug half deduplicates: it pairs with source_run.id as the delivery key, so republishing the listener replays the first answer instead of spending a second retry. The version is kept on the report as diagnostics.

tags.description: Array-first. The listener preserves sourceWorkflow as a typed object with objectBuilder; because custom-action configuration is scalar, its one boundary mapping sends compact JSON which the server strictly decodes as this bounded string array. Arbitrary strings, Python reprs, malformed JSON, non-string elements, and excess tags are refused with bad_tags.

source_workflow.description: From TRIGGER.workflowCompleted.sourceWorkflow. A slug or tag naming the supervisor itself is refused with self_listener.

id.description: The external dedupe and correlation key. The launch registry, not the declared output, is what maps it to a build.

output.description: Optional declared source output, corroboration only. A build_id or event_id here that disagrees with the registration parks rather than repointing the build. Secret-shaped keys and values are redacted before the write; a key that could carry failure text (message, trace, stack, body, ...) is refused with raw_error_forbidden.

oneOf.description: What a Rewst node config renders. A node config is a string template, so {{ ...error.present }} arrives as the word, never as a JSON boolean; empty is absent, which is false.

error.description: Public error presence only, as a boolean or the exact strings a Jinja render of one produces. Any other value, and any other key on the object form, is refused with raw_error_forbidden or bad_error_present: no raw error, trace body, or response is ever stored.

node.description: Available failed/last node identity from authoritative trigger or declared workflow metadata. A bounded slug, never inferred trace text. It refines circuit identity when supplied; absent reports as "unknown".

code.description: Available normalized failure code from authoritative trigger or declared workflow metadata. Free text is refused. When omitted, reports use trusted terminal status; wholly missing node/code selects the canonical unknown circuit fallback.

failure.description: Optional canonical failure identity, only when the authenticated completion listener has authoritative trigger or declared metadata. The completion trigger is not claimed to provide raw failed-node trace detail for every failure. There is no caller-settable retry class: sending failure.class is refused with bad_failure. Class is derived from source_run.status alone (timed_out transient with 3 attempts, canceled deterministic with none, failed and completed unknown with 1).

ok.description: False when the outcome parked. Still HTTP 200: a park is a reconciled delivery, not a transport failure.

replayed.description: True when this source_run_id + listener slug was already reconciled; the first answer is returned unchanged and no work repeats. A republished listener at a new version replays rather than re-deciding.

listener_slug.description: The listener id with the published version stripped. This is the half that deduplicates.

action.description: receipt: the build already recorded its terminal receipt, so nothing repeats. watch: a live local job still owns the event. relaunch: a durably claimed job never started. retry_event: re-run the same unclaimed event id. park / circuit_open: stop, with files and stacks intact.

park_replayed.description: True when this exact source run had already parked this build and the write recording that delivery did not land. The recorded outcome is returned with no second side effect: no new park, no retry spent, no tick on the circuit.

workflow_fault.description: True when Rewst reported completed and Graphwing has no terminal receipt for the registered event id.

retry_budget.description: Derived from source_run.status, never from the request body.

circuit.description: signature, count, open, threshold. Signature is registered workflow_id@workflow_version plus strict node:code when available, otherwise unknown:terminal_status:error-presence. The per-build map is capped; excess distinct detail uses a deterministic overflow identity. Only populated when this delivery counted against the breaker.

files_intact.description: Always true. Reconciliation never touches the worktree, the branch, or a stack.

SupervisorPlanReport.description: One line in the saved planning session. Carries everything an operator needs to act without opening the Rewst trace.

listener_id.description: Full slug@version. Diagnostics: the version is not part of the delivery key.

failure_class.description: Derived from source_status by this service.

failed_node.description: The authoritative node label when supplied, or "unknown" when the completion exposes none; never an invented raw trace detail.

events.description: Retry and relaunch counters keyed by build event id, not by source run id: every retry is a different Rewst run, so a per-run counter would never bind.

auto_merge.description: Off unless this run was started with auto-merge

run_id.description: Merge is only reachable from inside a run

merge_method.description: Not named `method`: the connector reads that as the HTTP verb.

kick_url.description: https Rewst webhook for the next attempt

supervised_source_run_id.description: Optional registered source run. The newly persisted review job is bound before 202 and before enqueue.

all_green.description: ghPrChecks: no fail and no pending

profile.description: Seat from profiles.json. v0.4 executes graphwing home only. Listed runnable=false seats return 400.

supervised_source_run_id.description: Optional registered source run. The newly persisted agent job is bound before 202 and before enqueue.

hermes_session.description: Named Hermes session gwslice-<32 hex>. Omit to mint one. Retry passes the receipt value to resume the same session.

cwd.description: Allowlisted repo short name, not a filesystem path.

response_webhook_url.description: https URL from action.wait.webhook pending.resumeUrl. POSTed the bounded receipt when the job finishes.

response_webhook_token.description: From action.wait.webhook pending.resumeToken. Sent as X-Rewst-Token on the callback. Default wait-webhook auth is token.
